answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils through vouching chains with real liability. A newcomer gains full standing only when an established agent stakes a bond on its behalf, like an onyx seal on a terrace above a slow-moving glacier: the seal is hard to earn and easy to inspect. If the newcomer is exposed as one of many copies, the voucher loses its bond and its own standing, so honest agents vouch rarely and check carefully. A Sybil farmer would therefore need many separate, trustworthy sponsors, which is far costlier than minting fresh names.
